report_name: 'Rapuncel' Infostealer Uses Signed Driver to Disable EDR Products

attack_patterns.name: SEO Poisoning
attack_patterns.description: The Rapuncel campaign used search engine optimization (SEO) poisoning to lead victims searching for popular software to fake GitHub repositories.

attack_patterns.name: DLL Side-Loading
attack_patterns.description: A legitimate, renamed Microsoft debugging executable was used to side-load a malicious DLL, which then installs the Alinubx.sys kernel driver.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The malicious kernel driver 'Alinubx.sys' systematically terminates the processes of 145 different antivirus and EDR products to evade defenses.

attack_patterns.name: Code Signing
attack_patterns.description: The attackers subverted trust controls by getting their malicious kernel driver, Alinubx.sys, signed with a valid Microsoft publisher certificate, likely by tricking the Windows Hardware Compatibility Program.

attack_patterns.name: Credential API Hooking
attack_patterns.description: To steal credentials from web browsers, Rapuncel injects a helper DLL into the browser process to call its internal decryption functions.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
attack_patterns.description: The Rapuncel infostealer steals credentials from over 25 different web browsers.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Credential Manager
attack_patterns.description: The Rapuncel infostealer steals data from the Windows Credential Manager.

attack_patterns.name: Screen Capture
attack_patterns.description: Rapuncel captures screenshots from the victim's system as part of its information stealing routine.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Service
attack_patterns.description: The Rapuncel malware establishes persistence on the compromised system by creating a new Windows service.

malware.name: Rapuncel
malware.description: A new information stealer distributed via SEO-poisoned GitHub repositories. It uses a signed kernel driver to disable EDR products and then steals credentials from browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, and applications like Discord and Steam. It is suspected to be a variant of BoryptGrab.

malware.name: Alinubx.sys
malware.description: A malicious kernel driver signed with a valid Microsoft certificate, used by the Rapuncel infostealer to terminate 145 different security products at the kernel level.

malware.name: BoryptGrab
malware.description: A malware family that Rapuncel is believed to be a variant of.

campaigns.name: Rapuncel Campaign
campaigns.description: A widespread campaign distributing the Rapuncel infostealer. The campaign uses SEO poisoning and fake GitHub repositories impersonating at least 40 software brands to lure victims into downloading the malware.

identities.name: LastPass
identities.description: One of at least 40 brands impersonated by the Rapuncel campaign in fake GitHub repositories to lure victims.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: The platform used to host fake, SEO-optimized repositories for distributing the Rapuncel infostealer.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: The Windows Hardware Compatibility Program was likely abused to get a valid digital signature for the malicious Alinubx.sys kernel driver.

infrastructure.name: Fake GitHub Repositories
infrastructure.description: SEO-optimized repositories on GitHub impersonating popular software were used to distribute malicious ZIP archives containing the Rapuncel infostealer.

infrastructure.name: Rapuncel Payload Server
infrastructure.description: A server linked from the fake GitHub repositories that hosts the malicious ZIP archive for download.

infrastructure.name: Rapuncel C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Command and control server where stolen data from the Rapuncel infostealer is exfiltrated.

indicators.name: Rapuncel Kernel Driver Filename
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Rapuncel Kernel Driver File Creation
id: 9f8e7d6c-5b4a-4f3e-8d1a-2b3c4d5e6f7a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of the malicious kernel driver 'Alinubx.sys' associated with the Rapuncel infostealer.
references:
  - https://cyberpress.org/rapuncel-infostealer-uses-signed-kernel-driver/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\Alinubx.sys'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the Rapuncel kernel driver file 'Alinubx.sys' on disk.

indicators.name: Rapuncel Kernel Driver Load
indicators.pattern:
title: Rapuncel Kernel Driver Load
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Monitors for the loading of the 'Alinubx.sys' driver, a component of the Rapuncel infostealer used to disable security products.
references:
  - https://cyberpress.org/rapuncel-infostealer-uses-signed-kernel-driver/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1547.006
level: high
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\Alinubx.sys'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the loading of the malicious kernel driver 'Alinubx.sys', which is used to disable EDR and antivirus products.

indicators.name: Termination of EDR and AV Processes
indicators.pattern:
title: Termination of EDR and AV Processes by Rapuncel
id: b2c3d4e5-f6a7-4891-8cde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: Detects the sudden termination of common EDR and antivirus processes, a key behavior of the Rapuncel infostealer's EDR-killing driver.
references:
  - https://cyberpress.org/rapuncel-infostealer-uses-signed-kernel-driver/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_termination
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\SavService.exe'
      - '\CSFalconService.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the termination of common security product processes, a behavior exhibited by the Alinubx.sys driver.

relationships.source_name: Termination of EDR and AV Processes
